summary: A rhizomatous fern whose broad, divided fronds arch over damp sheltered ground. It supplies concealment and bedding, while decaying fronds feed babosa. Bruised foliage leaves a scent clue in still air; living green growth ends where cave light becomes insufficient (F8, F9, F16, F18).

chains.trait: Broad fronds supported by a creeping rhizome
links: Humid woodland and spray fringes reduce drying stress beneath shelter.
Broad divided fronds intercept diffuse light reaching the ground.
A creeping rhizome stores reserves and replaces damaged fronds.
Spreading colonies trap litter and create shaded ground cover.
chains.play: Gather detached fronds for bedding or move through patches under cover; disturbed fronds may reveal passage.
chains.weakness: Fronds wilt on exposed dry ground and tear in strong wind; stored reserves cannot sustain indefinite growth in darkness.
observe: Fronds spread broadly beneath trees but shrink near an exposed clearing.
Curled new fronds rise beside an older broken stalk.
Green colonies thin toward a cave's permanently dark interior.

plausibility.summary: The fern occupies humid shelter with sufficient light. Rhizomes permit recovery after damage but do not turn a photosynthetic plant into a deep-cave producer.

analogues.mechanism: Persistent rhizomes bear successive fronds and support vegetative spread; fern structure is covered in [Gifford and Foster's vascular-plant text](https://openlibrary.org/books/OL2050530M/Morphology_and_evolution_of_vascular_plants).

chains.trait: Underside spore clusters with moisture-dependent establishment
links: Small spores develop in clusters beneath mature fronds.
Drying intervals release spores into local air movement; splash redistributes some nearby.
Spores reaching damp illuminated surfaces can establish a reproductive stage.
Persistent moisture allows fertilization and recruitment beside existing colonies.
chains.play: Inspect frond undersides to identify reproductive patches and follow new growth along damp, lit cave margins.
chains.weakness: Continuous wetting delays dry release; spores stranded in dark or drying sites fail to establish.
observe: Mature frond undersides carry orderly brown spore clusters.
A drying fertile frond sheds fine dust when disturbed.
Small recruits occupy damp light gaps rather than the black cave floor.

plausibility.summary: Spore transport uses air movement and water, not the molecular-diffusion rule for scent. Earth-like reproductive structures are functional analogues within the seeded biochemistry.

analogues.mechanism: Sporangia release spores, while the separate gametophyte stage depends on suitable moisture; see [Gifford and Foster](https://openlibrary.org/books/OL2050530M/Morphology_and_evolution_of_vascular_plants).

poison.signal: Ordinary shaded foliage is green; absence of red veins does not establish edibility.

gameplay.cover: Dense arching fronds conceal low-moving creatures and obscure footprints.
gameplay.notes: Bruising releases a green scent that persists best in still sheltered air (F16). It neither directs spores nor carries reliably through wind.

relations.note: Consumes softened decaying fronds and returns nutrients to the litter.
Frond arches conceal its low prowling posture at woodland and cave edges.
Collects detached bedding and reads broken stalks or bruised scent as passage clues.
Occupies moist shaded ground beneath the fog-drip canopy.
Shares illuminated damp entrance fringes without producing its own light.
Dead fronds provide substrate for decomposition.

generator.trunk: No aerial trunk; creeping shallow rhizome beneath litter.

branching.buttress: None; rhizome and fine roots anchor each patch.

leaf.arrangement: Loose crowns repeated along a creeping rhizome

overlay_rules: Young unfurling fronds are pale green.
Mature fertile undersides bear brown spore clusters.
Dead fronds fade ochre-brown; no luminous overlay.

placement.slope: Sheltered banks and benches up to about 40 degrees; exclude active scour channels
placement.wetness: Continuously humid, drained ground with intermittent spray
placement.soil: Humus-rich volcanic soil and moist tuff pockets
placement.fog: Favours fog-drip shelter and waterfall humidity.
placement.density: Overlapping colonies interrupted by exposed rock, deep shade and active water.

generator.seasonal: Flushes during moist mild periods; drought browns outer fronds while sheltered rhizomes persist.
generator.wind_response: Fronds flutter and bow in weak currents; exposed fronds split or collapse in gales.

journal.en: Soft feathers cover the wet ground. They stop where the cave loses its light.
journal.es: Plumas blandas cubren el suelo húmedo. Se detienen donde la cueva pierde la luz.

observe: Compare a damp green cave mouth with the fern-free darkness beyond.
Look under mature fronds for ordered spore clusters.
Watch a displaced frond settle over a concealed merodeador trail.
secrets: A continuous fern bed can hide a narrow low passage used by merodeador.
Fresh bruising is easiest to detect before wind or waterfall turbulence disperses the scent.
